product.name: BPC-157 (Arginine)
product.description:
BPC-157 is a synthetic peptide fragment derived from a larger body protection compound studied for its interactions with cellular signaling, angiogenesis pathways, and tissue integrity models. It has been explored in laboratory settings examining peptide stability, endothelial signaling, and inflammatory marker modulation.

Note:  This product is supplied in capsule form for laboratory research, analytical evaluation, and formulation studies. Capsule format is provided strictly for controlled research handling and material consistency, not for ingestion. Capsule format does not imply suitability for oral administration.
product.otherNames:
Body Protection Compound-157
Pentadecapeptide BPC 157
BPC 157
product.sequence: Gly-Glu-Pro-Pro-Pro-Gly-Lys-Pro-Ala-Asp-Asp-Ala-Gly-Leu-Val (GEPPPGKPADDAGLV) - linear, 15 residues, no disulfide bridges or cyclisation
product.technicalOverview:
BPC-157 is a synthetic pentadecapeptide corresponding to a partial sequence of a cytoprotective protein originally identified in human gastric juice. The identifiers above describe the free peptide; this product is supplied as the arginine salt, which alters the formula weight of the material as weighed but not the identity of the peptide itself.

Structurally it is notable for an unusually high proline content, including three consecutive proline residues at positions 3-5, which confers conformational rigidity on the N-terminal segment and is associated with the peptide's reported stability in gastric juice - a property that distinguishes it from most linear peptides of similar length.

Mechanistically, the published preclinical work is diffuse rather than convergent: reported observations include modulation of angiogenic signalling and VEGF-receptor pathways, interaction with the nitric oxide system, upregulation of growth hormone receptor expression in cultured tendon fibroblasts, and changes in inflammatory mediator profiles. No single, well-characterised molecular target has been established, and the breadth of reported effects is itself a reason for caution when interpreting the literature.

The honest framing on evidence quality: nearly the entire body of evidence is preclinical - rodent and in vitro work, a substantial fraction of it originating from a small number of research groups in a single research tradition. Recent systematic and narrative reviews in the orthopaedic and sports-medicine literature examined the human evidence directly and found no adequately powered, well-controlled clinical trials; the human reports that exist are small case series without control arms. Human efficacy and safety therefore remain uncharacterised, as does oral bioavailability, which is a separate open question for a capsule format. The claims attached to this molecule should be read as hypotheses generated by animal work, not as established results.
product.researchApplications:
Rodent models of gastrointestinal, tendon, ligament and muscle injury
In vitro angiogenesis and endothelial cell migration assays
Growth-factor receptor expression studies in cultured fibroblasts
Nitric oxide pathway and vascular signalling investigations
Inflammatory marker and cytokine profiling in cell culture
Peptide stability, solid-state formulation and dissolution studies
Analytical reference-standard comparison and HPLC / LC-MS method development
product.storageHandling: Store the sealed capsule bottle at controlled room temperature (15-25 C / 59-77 F) in a dry place, away from direct light and humidity. For extended storage, refrigeration at 2-8 C in a sealed, desiccated container is preferred. Do not reconstitute - this is a solid dosage form and is not intended for dissolution or injection. Keep the desiccant in the bottle and close it promptly after handling; peptides in solid form are hygroscopic and moisture uptake is the main driver of degradation. Handle with gloves in a clean, dry laboratory area. For Research Use Only - not for human or animal consumption.

related.name: 5AMINO1MQ — Redox Signaling Reference Compound (RUO)
related.description:
5-Amino-1MQ is a small-molecule NNMT pathway inhibitor studied for its role in cellular energy regulation and metabolic signaling research models. It is frequently utilized in investigations involving adipocyte metabolism and NAD+-related pathways. 

Chloride

Research Use Only.
related.compoundClass: Small-molecule quinolinium salt; nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT) inhibitor
related.otherNames:
5-Amino-1-methylquinolinium chloride
5-Amino-1MQ
5-amino-1-methylquinolinium
Note: registry 42464-96-0 is used by most suppliers for the chloride, but is also cited for the iodide salt; identifiers here describe the CHLORIDE.
related.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
5-Amino-1MQ is a permanently charged quinolinium cation supplied as its chloride salt. It is a substrate-site inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), the cytosolic enzyme that methylates nicotinamide to 1-methylnicotinamide using S-adenosylmethionine as the methyl donor. Because that reaction consumes nicotinamide, NNMT activity sits directly upstream of the salvage route into NAD+; inhibiting it is the reason the compound appears in NAD+ and cellular-energy literature rather than any direct action on NAD+ itself.

A note on identity: the CAS number 42464-96-0 is quoted by many suppliers for the chloride, but that registry number resolves to the iodide salt (C10H11N2·I, MW 286.11) in Sigma-Aldrich's catalogue and in ChemicalBook's own property block. Because the two assignments conflict, no CAS is asserted here for the chloride. The molecular formula and weight above describe the chloride salt as supplied.

Evidence is preclinical. The most-cited work (Neelakantan et al., 2018) reported that membrane-permeable small-molecule NNMT inhibitors of this class reduced adiposity in diet-induced obese mice; there are no controlled human outcome data. Interpret any metabolic claim accordingly.
related.researchApplications: Used as a tool compound for NNMT enzyme-inhibition assays, methylation-flux and 1-methylnicotinamide quantification work, and adipocyte differentiation and lipid-accumulation models. Also used in NAD+ salvage-pathway studies where the goal is to raise nicotinamide availability by blocking its methylation rather than by supplementing a precursor. Common readouts are LC-MS/MS measurement of 1-methylnicotinamide and SAM/SAH ratios, cellular NAD+ pools, and adipocyte lipid staining.
related.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat. Keep any desiccant in the bottle and re-close tightly after each opening — capsule shells take up atmospheric moisture and will soften or stick together in humid conditions. Do not refrigerate; condensation on return to room temperature is the usual cause of capsule degradation. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.

related.name: AKKERMANSIA
related.description:
Akkermansia muciniphila is a commensal bacterial strain frequently studied in gut microbiome research. Investigations often explore its role in mucosal barrier integrity, metabolic signaling, and host-microbe interactions.

Research Use Only.
related.compoundClass: Gut commensal bacterium — Akkermansia muciniphila (phylum Verrucomicrobiota); anaerobic mucin-degrading species
related.otherNames: Akkermansia muciniphila; A. muciniphila; mucin-degrading gut commensal
related.sequence: Not applicable — Akkermansia muciniphila is a bacterium, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
Akkermansia muciniphila is an oval, non-motile, strictly anaerobic bacterium first described by Derrien and colleagues in 2004. It was isolated from human faeces and characterised by its unusual metabolic niche: it uses host-secreted intestinal mucin as its sole source of carbon and nitrogen, and it colonises the mucus layer overlying the epithelium rather than the lumen. It is a normal member of the adult human gut community, typically making up a low single-digit percentage of total faecal bacteria.

Interest in the organism comes from repeated observations that its relative abundance is lower in obesity, type 2 diabetes and inflammatory bowel conditions, and from rodent work linking colonisation to mucus-layer thickness and barrier function. A proof-of-concept human study (Depommier et al., Nature Medicine 2019) administered live and pasteurised A. muciniphila to overweight and obese volunteers over three months; it was designed to test feasibility and safety rather than to demonstrate efficacy, and its metabolic findings were exploratory.

The evidence base has since become more nuanced rather than more certain. A 2025 Cell Metabolism trial reported that the response to supplementation depended on the participant's own baseline Akkermansia level, which is a reminder that this is a colonisation-dependent intervention, not a dose-response drug. Potency here is expressed in AFU (active fluorescent units), a flow-cytometry count of intact cells, which is not interchangeable with the CFU counts used for culturable probiotics.
related.researchApplications: Used in gut-microbiome composition and intervention studies, intestinal barrier and mucus-layer integrity models, and host–microbe signalling work involving the Amuc_1100 outer-membrane protein and TLR2. Typical readouts are 16S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic quantification of relative abundance, faecal and mucosal colonisation, short-chain fatty acid profiles, tight-junction protein expression, and circulating markers of endotoxaemia.
related.storageHandling: Refrigerate at 2–8 °C (36–46 °F) in the sealed original bottle; viability and the stated AFU count are time- and temperature-dependent, and warm or humid storage will degrade the count well before the printed date. Keep away from light and moisture, keep the desiccant in the bottle, and re-close tightly. Do not freeze. Because this is a live/pasteurised bacterial preparation rather than a chemical, do not repackage into unlabelled containers, and handle with the same care as any other biological material in the laboratory.

related.name: ATX-304 (Testing pending at ILS)
related.description:
ATX-304 is a small-molecule pan-AMPK activator of the benzothiazole class (also referenced as O-304 / OS-01), originated by Betagenon AB. It is not a peptide. It is studied in laboratory research for direct allosteric activation of AMP-activated protein kinase and the downstream effects on cellular energy sensing, glucose uptake and mitochondrial substrate handling.

For Research Use Only (RUO). Not for human or animal use.
related.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
ATX-304 is a synthetic small molecule, not a peptide. Product copy in this category sometimes describes it as a peptide analogue acting on angiogenic signalling; that is incorrect. It is an orally bioavailable benzothiazole originally developed as O304 at Umeå University and Betagenon AB, and it is classed as a first-in-class direct pan-activator of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK).

Mechanistically it does not mimic AMP at the γ-subunit nucleotide sites. It raises AMPK activity by suppressing dephosphorylation of the activation-loop residue Thr172, so phosphorylated AMPK persists longer; a mitochondrial uncoupling contribution has also been reported. Because it activates all AMPK heterotrimer combinations rather than one isoform, downstream effects span skeletal muscle glucose uptake, hepatic lipid handling and microvascular perfusion.

The evidence is early-stage. Steneberg et al. (JCI Insight, 2018) reported improved glucose homeostasis and microvascular perfusion in diet-induced obese mice and, in a small phase IIa proof-of-concept cohort of type 2 diabetes patients already on metformin, reductions in fasting plasma glucose and HOMA-IR. A later study in aged mice reported improvements in metabolic and cardiac function and exercise capacity. There are no completed large controlled efficacy trials, and no approved indication.
related.researchApplications: Used as a direct AMPK-activating tool compound in skeletal muscle and hepatocyte energy-metabolism models, mitochondrial bioenergetics work, and microvascular perfusion studies. Typical readouts are phospho-AMPK (Thr172) and phospho-ACC immunoblotting, cellular oxygen consumption and extracellular acidification rates, glucose uptake in myotubes, and in vivo glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity testing. Also used as a comparator against indirect activators such as metformin and AICAR.
related.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat. Keep any desiccant in the bottle and re-close tightly after each opening; capsule shells absorb atmospheric moisture and will soften or stick in humid conditions. Do not refrigerate. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.

related.name: ATX-304 Blend
related.description:
This blended formulation contains a small-molecule AMPK activator and multiple additional small-molecule and nutrient-derived compounds studied in laboratory research for their involvement in metabolic signaling, cellular energy regulation, and oxidative pathway models.

ATX-304 (OS-01) is examined in research settings for its interaction with cellular signaling pathways associated with tissue-level metabolic regulation. 5-Amino-1MQ is studied for its involvement in nicotinamide metabolism and energy-associated intracellular signaling pathways. Myo-Inositol and D-Chiro-Inositol are investigated in laboratory models for their roles in insulin-related signaling cascades and phosphatidylinositol-mediated cellular communication. Chromium Picolinate is examined for its interaction with glucose-associated signaling mechanisms and trace mineral–dependent metabolic models. N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) is studied for its involvement in redox balance, glutathione synthesis pathways, and oxidative stress signaling models.

This material is supplied in capsule format for analytical testing and non-clinical investigational research applications. Capsule format is provided solely to support controlled handling and material consistency in laboratory environments.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Multi-ingredient research blend — direct AMPK activator, NNMT inhibitor and inositol stereoisomers
related.sequence: Not applicable — multi-ingredient blend of small molecules, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
This is a four-component blend, so no single CAS number, formula or molecular weight describes it. Each component is summarised below.

ATX-304 (also called O-304 or OS-01) is a synthetic benzothiazole small molecule, CAS 1261289-04-6, formula C16H11Cl2N3O2S. It is a direct pan-activator of AMP-activated protein kinase that works by suppressing dephosphorylation of AMPK at Thr172. Preclinical work reported improved glucose homeostasis and microvascular perfusion in obese mice, with a small phase IIa signal in type 2 diabetes patients on metformin. Note that it is a small molecule, not a peptide analogue.

5-Amino-1MQ is a quinolinium salt and a substrate-site inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT). Blocking NNMT prevents methylation of nicotinamide to 1-methylnicotinamide, which is why it appears in NAD+ salvage-pathway and adipocyte-metabolism literature. Evidence is preclinical.

Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are naturally occurring cyclitol stereoisomers and the precursors of the inositol phosphoglycan second messengers that sit downstream of the insulin receptor. They are studied together, usually at a fixed ratio, in insulin-signalling and ovarian-function research. They are nutrient-derived compounds rather than novel chemical entities.

The components have not been studied as a combination in controlled work; anything said about the blend is an inference from the single-agent literature, not a finding about the blend itself.
related.researchApplications: Used in combined AMPK-activation and NAD+/methylation-flux models where the intent is to engage two independent nodes of cellular energy regulation at once, alongside inositol-mediated insulin second-messenger signalling. Typical readouts are phospho-AMPK (Thr172) and phospho-ACC, LC-MS/MS quantification of 1-methylnicotinamide and cellular NAD+, inositol phosphoglycan signalling markers, and glucose uptake or insulin sensitivity endpoints. Because the components act through separate pathways, single-agent arms are needed to attribute any observed effect.
related.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat. The inositol content is hygroscopic, so keep the desiccant in the bottle, re-close tightly after each opening, and avoid humid storage — moisture ingress will cause capsules to soften, stick or clump. Do not refrigerate. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.

related.name: Aicar — Redox Signaling Reference Compound (RUO)
related.description:
AICAR (5-Aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide) is a synthetic small molecule studied in laboratory research for its interaction with AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling pathways and intracellular energy regulation models. Research investigations commonly examine its role in metabolic pathway modulation, nucleotide metabolism, and downstream transcriptional signaling mechanisms in non-clinical environments.

This material is supplied for analytical testing, pathway evaluation, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Format is provided solely to support controlled laboratory handling and material consistency.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Purine nucleoside analogue; AMP mimetic and indirect AMPK activator
related.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
AICAR, also called acadesine or AICA riboside, is a nucleoside analogue of the purine biosynthesis intermediate 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide. Note the nomenclature carefully: the material supplied here is the riboside (nucleoside), not the ribotide monophosphate that shares the AICAR acronym in purine-pathway textbooks. The riboside is the cell-permeable form used experimentally.

Once inside the cell, adenosine kinase phosphorylates it to ZMP, which mimics AMP at the γ-subunit nucleotide-binding sites of AMP-activated protein kinase. That makes AICAR an indirect AMPK activator: it does not bind the kinase's catalytic site, it raises the apparent AMP:ATP signal. Because ZMP is a promiscuous AMP mimic it also acts on other AMP-sensitive enzymes, which is the main confounder in interpreting AICAR experiments and the reason direct activators are often run alongside it.

AICAR became widely cited after Narkar et al. (Cell, 2008) reported that it increased running endurance in sedentary mice, the work that introduced the term exercise mimetic. That study is a rodent finding; it is not evidence of a comparable effect in humans, and AICAR has no approved indication.
related.researchApplications: Standard positive-control activator in AMPK signalling assays and a widely used tool in skeletal muscle glucose-uptake, fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis models. Also used in purine nucleotide metabolism work and in ischaemia-reperfusion models. Typical readouts are phospho-AMPK (Thr172) and phospho-ACC immunoblotting, intracellular ZMP measurement by LC-MS, GLUT4 translocation, oxygen consumption rate, and PGC-1α expression. Because ZMP acts on multiple AMP-sensitive enzymes, AMPK-null or dominant-negative controls are needed to attribute effects to AMPK.
related.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat. AICAR is a hygroscopic nucleoside — keep the desiccant in the bottle, re-close tightly after each opening, and avoid humid storage. Do not refrigerate the capsules; condensation on return to room temperature is the usual cause of degradation. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.
related.citations: Narkar, Downes, Yu, et al. AMPK and PPARδ Agonists Are Exercise Mimetics. Cell. 2008;134(3):405-415. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2008.06.051

related.name: BAM 15 — Redox Signaling Reference Compound (RUO)
related.description:
BAM15 is a synthetic small molecule studied in laboratory research for its activity as a mitochondrial uncoupling agent and its interaction with cellular bioenergetics pathways. Research investigations commonly focus on its effects on mitochondrial membrane potential, oxidative phosphorylation models, and energy expenditure signaling mechanisms.

This material is supplied in capsule format for analytical testing, reference standard comparison, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Capsule format is provided solely to support controlled handling and material consistency in laboratory environments.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
BAM15 is a synthetic protonophore that dissipates the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane, uncoupling substrate oxidation from ATP synthesis. Electron transport continues while ATP output falls, so the energy is released as heat and oxygen consumption rises.

The reason BAM15 is used in preference to classical uncouplers such as DNP and FCCP is selectivity. It is reported to depolarise the mitochondrial inner membrane without a corresponding effect on the plasma membrane, which widens the window between the concentration that uncouples mitochondria and the concentration that is cytotoxic. That property is the whole point of the molecule and it is the correct thing to test for in any new model system, since the margin is cell-type dependent.

Evidence is preclinical. Alexopoulos et al. (Nature Communications, 2020) reported that BAM15 reduced fat mass and improved insulin sensitivity in diet-induced obese mice without reducing food intake or affecting body temperature. There are no human efficacy or safety trials. Uncouplers as a chemical class have a serious historical safety record — DNP caused fatal hyperthermia in the 1930s and continues to do so in illicit use — and that history is the correct frame for handling anything in this class.
related.researchApplications: Used as a selective mitochondrial uncoupling tool in bioenergetics work: Seahorse extracellular flux assays (as an alternative to FCCP for measuring maximal respiratory capacity), mitochondrial membrane potential measurement with TMRM or JC-1, and studies of reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial calcium handling and ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Also used in energy-expenditure and substrate-partitioning models. Dose-ranging against a plasma-membrane potential readout is advisable in any new cell type.
related.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, protected from light and heat. Keep the desiccant in the bottle and re-close tightly after each opening. Do not refrigerate. Handle as a potent research chemical: avoid generating or inhaling dust if capsules are opened, do not repackage into unlabelled containers, and keep well away from children and animals — mitochondrial uncouplers as a class have a narrow margin between an active and a dangerous exposure.
related.citations: Alexopoulos, Chen, Brandon, et al. Mitochondrial uncoupler BAM15 reverses diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance in mice. Nature Communications. 2020;11(1). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-16298-2

related.description:

related.technicalOverview:
This is a two-component blend, so no single molecular identity, CAS number or molecular weight applies to the product as supplied. The identifiers for each component are documented separately on their individual product records.

BPC-157 is a synthetic 15-residue peptide (GEPPPGKPADDAGLV) corresponding to a partial sequence of a protein originally isolated from human gastric juice. In rodent and in vitro models it has been reported to influence angiogenic signalling, nitric oxide pathways, growth-factor receptor expression and inflammatory mediators. Its unusually proline-rich N-terminal segment (three consecutive prolines at positions 3-5) is associated with conformational rigidity and relative stability in gastric juice.

KPV is the C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (residues 11-13). In cell and animal models it has been reported to dampen NF-kappaB and MAP-kinase signalling and to reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine output in intestinal and epithelial systems. Unlike full-length alpha-MSH, KPV is described as lacking the motif required for melanocortin receptor binding, which is why it is studied as an anti-inflammatory fragment rather than a pigmentary agent.

The honest framing on evidence quality: for both components the published record is overwhelmingly preclinical. BPC-157's literature is dominated by rodent and in vitro work, much of it from a small number of research groups, and recent systematic and narrative reviews of its use in musculoskeletal contexts explicitly note the absence of adequately powered human clinical trials. KPV's evidence base is smaller still and is almost entirely cell-culture and rodent work. No human clinical trial evidence supports this combination, and none supports either component in an oral solid dosage form - oral bioavailability of both peptides is itself an open research question. Claims attached to this blend should be read as hypotheses generated by animal work, not as established results. Combination effects have not been characterised at all.

related.name: CIRCADI-X
related.description:
Circadi-X Restore — Circadian Signaling Research Blend Capsules

This blended formulation contains botanical extracts, phospholipids, fatty acids, and micronutrients studied in laboratory research for their involvement in circadian signaling, neuroendocrine regulation, and stress-response pathway models.

Research interest commonly focuses on how individual components interact with circadian gene expression, cortisol-associated signaling, and neuronal timing mechanisms.

This material is supplied in capsule format for analytical testing and non-clinical investigational research applications.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Multi-ingredient research blend — botanical extracts, phospholipids, fatty acids and micronutrients
related.otherNames: Circadi-X Restore; Circadian Signaling Research Blend
related.sequence: Not applicable — multi-ingredient blend of botanical extracts, lipids and micronutrients, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
CIRCADI-X is a proprietary multi-ingredient blend, so no single CAS number, molecular formula or molecular weight applies to it. The supplied product description identifies the categories of material present — botanical extracts, phospholipids, fatty acids and micronutrients — but does not name the individual constituents or their amounts, so the specific components cannot be described here. Ask the supplier for a full ingredient declaration with per-capsule quantities before designing any work around it.

What can be said about the categories: botanical extracts are chemically complex mixtures whose composition varies with plant part, extraction solvent and standardisation marker, so two lots of the same named extract are not interchangeable unless standardised to the same marker at the same percentage. Phospholipids such as phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylcholine are membrane lipids studied in neuronal signalling contexts. Fatty acids and micronutrients in this kind of formulation are typically included as cofactors for neurotransmitter and melatonin synthesis rather than as active agents in their own right.

The blend as a combination has not been characterised in controlled research. Any statement about circadian gene expression, cortisol signalling or neuronal timing derives from single-ingredient literature and does not transfer to the mixture without direct study.
related.researchApplications: Would sit in circadian-biology and neuroendocrine research contexts — core clock gene expression (BMAL1, CLOCK, PER, CRY), salivary or plasma cortisol rhythm profiling, dim-light melatonin onset, and actigraphy or polysomnography endpoints. Because the formulation is proprietary and its constituents are undeclared, any such work needs a full ingredient breakdown and single-ingredient control arms first; a blend cannot be attributed to a mechanism.
related.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat. Blends containing phospholipids and fatty acids are prone to oxidative rancidity, so protect from light and air, keep the desiccant in the bottle, and re-close tightly after each opening. Do not refrigerate. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.
